en: One, Two, or Three Days: Leave Room for Weather
zh: 一、二、三天：给天气留下余地
ja: 一日・二日・三日：天気の余白を残す

p.src: This diagram is not a compulsory Hakone checklist. It shows how much a day can hold without losing the way out. Give each day one anchor worth travelling for, one commitment that cannot move, and one optional branch to remove when wind, fog, rain, or suspension changes the mountain. A day trip can centre on the upper route and lake. With one night, lodge arrival and dinner enter the plan before another attraction. With two nights, railway, mountain and lake, and one old-road or highland branch can occupy separate days. The right edge of each lane is not a final sight; it is a working way off the mountain. Before adding anything, write down where you enter, where you must be by a fixed time, and which connection depends most on weather. If those three answers are unclear, the itinerary is already full.

caption.zh: 一天、一晚与两晚不是同一清单的长短版。每天只守一条主线、一个固定时刻和一条可用的离山路；天气变化时交换整天，不把删掉的站补回。
caption.ja: 日帰り、一泊、二泊は同じ一覧の長短版ではない。一日に一つの軸、固定時刻、使える下山路を守り、天候が変われば一日ごと交換して、削った場所を戻さない。
caption.en: One day, one night, and two nights are not short and long versions of one checklist. Keep one anchor, one fixed commitment, and one working exit per day; exchange whole days with weather and do not restore cut stops.

p.src: Attempt a clear-weather day crossing only when three conditions meet: an early entry from the Odawara or Yumoto side, a continuous operating route across the upper mountain, and an evening exit that does not depend on improvisation. From Gora, continue through Sounzan to Owakudani; if the ropeway, visibility, and your condition all support it, descend towards Togendai. Use the boat for one lake leg only and choose one south-shore focus, such as the shrine area or the checkpoint with Onshi Park. Decide before climbing whether lunch will be a seated meal or whether that time belongs to the crossing. Do not add a full museum, the old road, both shores, and shopping. The route is usable only when one missed departure still leaves a dependable way out.

caption.zh: 早云山至大涌谷的第一段索道。先看谷地、喷气孔与维护道路；富士山是否出现，不影响这段路的价值。
caption.ja: 早雲山から大涌谷へ向かう最初の区間。谷、噴気孔、管理路を先に見る。富士山が見えるかどうかで、この区間の価値は変わらない。
caption.en: The first ropeway section from Sounzan to Owakudani. Read the valley, fumaroles, and maintenance roads first; the value of this crossing does not depend on Mount Fuji appearing.

p.src: When strong wind, dense fog, or suspension disconnects ropeway and boat in the morning, stop chasing the old plan. Switch to one museum on the mountain railway, then choose a Yumoto meal, a confirmed day bath, or a direct departure. Even the rail-side Open-Air Museum needs an opening and return check; indoors does not mean open or reachable. JMA forecasts describe likely weather, warnings describe hazard, and Hakone's live page describes current transport. None replaces the others. During a warning, road problem, or wider suspension, cancel sightseeing and follow official instructions to shelter or leave.

p.src: With one night, the onsen stay is the itinerary's fixed point, not an extra after sightseeing. On reaching Yumoto, deal with the large bag and choose only one first-day stop along the railway. Then follow the property's entrance, pickup, and dinner instructions and arrive at the agreed time. If entry into Hakone is late, go directly to the ryokan instead of squeezing missed sights into dusk. At check-in, settle dinner, bath, breakfast, checkout, and next-morning pickup together; only the remaining time belongs to bathing and rest. After breakfast, use weather and live operation to choose the second day: upper mountain and lake when conditions hold, a museum or lower route when they do not. Work the departure deadline backwards from the onward reservation. This is not a shortened first day; it is a full overnight stay.

caption.zh: 把旅馆确认邮件当成当天最后一段交通的终点。按约定时段抵达，登记时一次确认晚餐、浴场、早餐、退房与次日接送。
caption.ja: 宿の予約確認を、その日の移動の終点として使う。指定時刻までに着き、夕食、浴場、朝食、チェックアウト、翌朝の送迎を一度に確かめる。
caption.en: Treat the ryokan confirmation as the endpoint of the day's transport. Arrive within the stated window, then confirm dinner, baths, breakfast, checkout, and next-morning pickup together.

p.src: An art-led trip still needs one principal museum per day. Much of the Open-Air Museum visit unfolds on outdoor paths, so give it the drier window; its shorter official route is an option, not a target speed. Pola Museum can suit a wetter period, but travel from the Gora or Sengokuhara side, waiting, lunch, rest, and the return all sit outside gallery time. Pola's visitor FAQ gives an average visit of about ninety minutes. That is not the time from lodging door to lodging door. Across two art-led days, place the Open-Air Museum on one and Pola or another highland museum on the other. Do not put two major museums, Owakudani, and the boat into the same day. A good museum day leaves enough attention and energy to find the way back and eat properly.

caption.zh: 雕刻之森的草坡、步道与山脊：四位向导先看清场地起伏和天气，再决定室外与室内展区的顺序。画面传达步行尺度，不对应一件特定作品。
caption.ja: 彫刻の森の芝生、園路、稜線。四人のガイドは敷地の起伏と天気を見てから、屋外と屋内の順序を決める。歩く尺度を伝える場面で、特定の作品を示すものではない。
caption.en: Lawns, paths, and ridges at the Open-Air Museum: the four guides read the slope and weather before choosing the order of outdoor and indoor galleries. The scene conveys walking scale and does not depict a specific work.

p.src: Two nights are not for restoring every sight that failed to fit earlier. Use them to change the order of three complete days. Day 1 follows the mountain railway to one streetscape or museum, then reaches the lodging on time. Day 2 holds the weather-dependent upper mountain and Lake Ashi. Day 3 chooses either the checkpoint, cedar avenue, and a piece of old road from the south shore, or one museum with the Sengokuhara highland. If Day 2 is wet and Day 3 clear, swap the whole days and do not restore deleted stops. One suitable base removes a packing cycle. Move to the lake or highland only when it genuinely reduces the next day's return journey.

caption.zh: 船离开桃源台后，北岸缩小，外轮山环住水面。先借湖岸判断方位；富士山出现与否不影响这段航程的价值。
caption.ja: 桃源台を離れると北岸が小さくなり、外輪山が水面を囲む。湖岸で位置を読み、富士山の有無だけを航路の価値にしない。
caption.en: After Togendai recedes, the outer ridges enclose the water. Use the shore to read the route; the crossing remains worthwhile whether Mount Fuji appears or not.

p.src: To reduce transfers and steep walking, first ask the traveller what creates strain: standing, steps, a long slope, a crowded vehicle, or repeated changes. Then choose one museum with verified facilities, one seated lunch, and one simple return. Pola Museum's current official pages identify a sloped entrance, internal lifts, wheelchair loans, and multipurpose toilets. Those are specific entrance and building features; they do not prove that the whole journey from lodging to gallery is step-free. The museum's transport from the Gora side is also subject to timetable, capacity, road, and weather conditions. For the actual date and need, check the bus or shuttle, drop-off point, entrance, seated rest, toilets, and return as separate links. Where necessary, replace one transfer with a taxi whose pickup and drop-off have been confirmed.

caption.zh: 雨天抵达POLA美术馆时，把接驳或巴士、下车点、坡道入口、馆内设施与返程分开确认。入口的坡道不代表从旅馆到展厅的整段路线都无台阶。
caption.ja: 雨の日にポーラ美術館へ着く時も、送迎またはバス、降車地点、傾斜路の入口、館内設備、帰路を別々に確かめる。入口の傾斜路だけで、宿から展示室まで全区間に段差がないとは言えない。
caption.en: For a rainy arrival at Pola Museum, verify the shuttle or bus, drop-off, sloped entrance, internal facilities, and return separately. The entrance slope does not make the complete journey from lodging to gallery step-free.

p.src: Put every part of the itinerary on one timeline and overfilling becomes visible. On reaching Yumoto, decide whether the bag will be delivered, stored, or carried; separately verify that the service covers the property and accepts it under that day's conditions. Reserve a real interval for a seated lunch and toilets. Waiting for transport is not the same as rest. On an overnight day, place the property's entrance, pickup, check-in, and dinner on the same line. On departure day, circle the last service that still connects to the onward journey, not merely the theoretical final departure. Between attractions, add station finding, waiting, walking, tickets, and short pauses instead of summing vehicle times. Use one test: if missing the next departure would endanger dinner, lodging arrival, or an onward booking, remove a stop. Do not make everyone walk faster.

caption.zh: 箱根汤本的进山时刻：山谷和登山电车已经在眼前，四位向导仍先把当天要用的东西从过夜行李中分出来。
caption.ja: 箱根湯本で山へ入る前のひととき。谷と登山電車が目の前にあっても、四人のガイドは宿泊用の荷物から、その日に使う物を先に分ける。
caption.en: The threshold at Hakone-Yumoto: with the valley and mountain train already in view, the four guides still separate the day's essentials from the overnight luggage first.

p.src: Make three checks instead of refreshing all day. The night before, read JMA's forecast and warnings, then save the lodging confirmation, first morning route, and way out. Before breakfast ends, open Hakone's live operation and congestion information, then check any bus, road, or facility notice outside that page's coverage. Immediately before committing to Sounzan, Owakudani, Togendai, or a lake connection, check the upper services, boat, and last usable alternative once more. A forecast answers what weather may develop; a warning answers what hazard exists; an operation page answers which link is moving now; a reservation answers when you must arrive. When they disagree, reorder the day around hazard, ability to leave, and booked obligations. Do not use a clear forecast to contradict a suspension, or a running train to dismiss a warning.

p.src: When the day slips, cut souvenir shopping, the second attraction, then the most weather-exposed connection. Keep safety checks, necessary rest, booked meals, and the route out. A day trip follows one line that conditions support; leave the rest for another visit. With one night, make the onsen property a destination. With two, use the spare day to adapt and choose only one old-road, lake-shore, or highland branch. A lower-strain day needs one access-checked facility, one seated meal, and one simple return. The best plan still works at dusk: you know the next step, can eat and rest, and reach the place where you are expected.
